title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas while operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not stop after the collision. This shows a failure in obstacle detection or avoidance, where a system deployed in public streets did not recognize or respond to a small animal in its path. It would have taken either better training of the perception model to detect small animals, or a decision to include small-animal avoidance in the vehicle's safety specifications and testing protocol.

A resident claimed the vehicle also failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this after reviewing vehicle data. Whether this additional claim reflects a second failure mode or a misperception is not established. The operator present in the vehicle did not intervene to prevent the collision, raising a separate question about the conditions under which human operators are expected to override autonomous systems.

Avride responded by excluding certain streets around the lake from its service area and committed to evaluating technological improvements through simulation. Whether these changes address the underlying detection failure or merely avoid the location is not established.

Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in Austin, Texas, triggering neighborhood backlash over the safety of self-driving cars. The incident occurred when the vehicle, which was in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present, hit the duck near Mueller Lake and did not stop. Residents had become attached to this particular duck, which was nesting outside a local restaurant, and have since preserved its eggs in an incubator. A resident also claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this claim after reviewing vehicle data.

Following the incident, Avride adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake from its service area. The company is now evaluating technological improvements through simulations to help prevent similar situations in the future while maintaining safety performance in other scenarios. Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating autonomously at the time of the incident and stated it found no evidence supporting the stop sign violation claim.
